newsitem.title: USA: Dade Cty, Fla., officials won't discuss grand jury.
newsitem.headline: Dade Cty, Fla., officials won't discuss grand jury.

text.p: Dade County finance officials who testified before a federal grand jury investigation bond-related corruption declined to comment on their testimony Tuesday.
County Manager Armando Vidal, Finance Director Ed Marquez and Bond Administrator Lidia Diaz were subpoenaed Friday to testify before the panel on Tuesday.
They did not return Reuter phone calls Tuesday but released the following prepared statement:

"Federal authorities have requested that Metro-Dade officials refrain from discussing aspects of this case with third parties. Metro-Dade will continue to fully cooperate with all regulatory and law enforcement agencies and therefore declines any comment on any matters pertaining to this investigation."

Last week, the U.S. Attorney's office subpoeaned county records pertaining to the methods used to choose underwriters for Dade County bond deals, and records pertaining to participation in those deals by the California firm Grigsby Brandford and Co Inc.

The Miami Herald has reported that the FBI had videotapes in which former firm president Calvin Grigsby allegedly discussed paying a kickback to county Commissioner James Burke, who headed the commission's finance committee, in exchange for steering deals to the firm.
Burke denied wrongdoing and said there was no bribe. He confirmed the existence of an FBI tape, but said the comments had been misinterpreted.

Grigsby could not be reached for comment. Grigsby's high-profile attorney Johnnie Cochran Jr said his client "strongly maintains his innocence." Grigsby has not been charged with any wrongdoing in the probe.
Federal investigators have declined to comment.
